The session cookie is SameSite=Lax; the MFA challenge cookie Strict, scoped to /login.
Both the session cookie (when Secure, that is in every production build) and the SSO binding cookie carry __Host- (KP11-78, Workflow 11F).

The API, the flow and the console are separate origins (three hosts in the chart, three ports on compose).

The chart's Ingress redirects HTTP to HTTPS on every host, the API host included, where the requirement asks an API not to redirect: the NGINX controllers refuse plain HTTP on one host only through a snippet annotation (KP11-81, open). The Gateway route on an HTTPS-only listener (gateway.httpRoute.parentRefs, KP11-84) refuses it; compose leaves TLS to the operator.
Forwarded addresses are read only from the trusted proxies OPENVERIFY_TRUST_PROXY names; trust-all makes production facts null; the flow server counts its trusted hops.
Message boundaries are Node's strict HTTP parser on each process; the operator's load balancer and ingress must agree on them (one HTTP version end to end, no ambiguous framing).

docs/security/vulnerability-policy.md gives the remediation time frames (critical 7 days, high 30, medium 90, low the next release), held by its record test; the allowlist's expiries are enforced by the supply-chain gate.

SBOMs are built (Syft, cdxgen, the CycloneDX Gradle plugin) but exist only as workflow artifacts until the first approved publication, whose publish job (wired in Workflow 11G, never run) attests each image's CycloneDX SBOM to its digest; KP11-39 is open.
Expensive features (graph queries, imports, exports, workflows, screenings) are documented with their limits and the measured figures.

Per-push scanners gate at high with an expiring allowlist; the image gate still fails on the Debian bases' findings that have no Debian fix and on Node 22.23.4's four highs fixed in 22.23.5, which turns 14 days old on 2026-11-25 (KP11-42, Workflow 11G's dependency review); release.yml's publish job waits for that gate, so a failing image gate publishes nothing.

Operator patterns run through the linear-time matcher or are refused (C252), and rate policies, timeouts and per-environment caps are in place; fairness on the shared queue missed at the default cap, 26.6 times idle (Workflow 11D review amendments item 1).
Images carry no test code or dev tooling: since Workflow 11F the API image no longer compiles face-scan:benchmark, a development tool (KP11-71; B7-T4).
Each resource is serialised by its own schema; masked fields stay masked without pii:view.
Outbound fetches follow no redirect except the stream client's one same-origin redirect where a publisher needs it.
Strict zod objects refuse members a route does not declare.
Client addresses come from OPENVERIFY_TRUST_PROXY's trusted proxies only; the operator sets the list (B1-D2).

TypeScript strict mode for every package through tsconfig.base.json, checked by the forced typecheck of each Validation; no test asserts the setting itself, and the Python and Kotlin code rely on mypy and the Kotlin compiler.

A body naming __proto__ or constructor.prototype is refused with 400 and pollutes no prototype; strict schemas refuse unknown members and the runner drops a guest's __proto__ key (KP11-72, Workflow 11F).
Query and body schemas take one value per member: a single-valued query parameter given twice is refused with 400, never read as one of its values (KP11-72, Workflow 11F).
docs/security/logging.md is the inventory of each process's logging, held to the configured redaction lists by its record test; that only the API and the worker redact is 16.2.5's gap (BX-I1).
pino lines carry time, level, request id and route; audit entries carry actor, action, object and time.
Timestamps are epoch milliseconds (UTC); keeping host clocks synchronised is the operator's (B4-S8).
Every process writes to stdout only, as the log inventory states; where the operator ships them is its store (16.4.3).

JSON lines (pino) for the API and the worker only; vision logs through Python logging and uvicorn's plain-text access log, and no test shows the console's, the flow server's or the code runner's format (the 11F documentation review, C274.3; KP11-74).
The API and the worker redact personal keys and paths; the console, flow server, vision and runner have no redaction list (BX-I1, Workflow 11F).
Every sign-in, step-up and session end is an audit entry; a refused sign-in is counted by the limiter and logged as a code, not audited.
A refused authorisation answers 403 or the generic 404 and is in the request log by route and status; it is not an audit entry.
Limiter refusals and store failures are logged with a metric; schema refusals are not logged as security events.
Unexpected errors are logged by class and code; insecure transport logs a warning, and an unavailable limiter store a warning with metric: rate_limiter_store_unavailable.

pino writes JSON with escaped strings in the API and the worker; vision's uvicorn access log writes the request path as plain text and its tracebacks raw, so log injection is not shown to be prevented there (the 11F documentation review, C274.3; KP11-74).

Audit entries are append-only in the database (retention deletes only past the environment's setting, measured from the time the caller states, B3-R4); log files and their access are the operator's store.
Shipping logs and audit entries to a separate system is the operator's (G-LOGINV).
